newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says catches top-ranking rocket spy.
newsitem.headline: Russia says catches top-ranking rocket spy.

text.p: Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) has caught a senior officer in the strategic missile command who was preparing to sell defence secrets to a foreign power, Russian news agencies said on Tuesday.
The reports gave no further details, nor did they say to which country the officer planned to pass the material. FSB officials were not immediately available for comment.
Tass quoted sources at the FSB, which succeeded the Soviet KGB, as saying the treachery might have badly damaged Russia's defences and cost tens of millions of dollars.

The officer, caught in the past few days, had been charged with treason, which carries the death penalty. The Russian armed forces are suffering from a severe cash crisis that has left officers' morale and living conditions plumbing the depths.
Despite the end of the Cold War, espionage still goes on actively between Russia and her former foes.
In the latest case in Washinton, Harold Nicholson, a high-ranking CIA officer, pleaded guilty this month to conspiring to sell U.S. defence secrets to Moscow since 1994.
FBI agent Earl Pitts also admitted spying for the Soviet Union and then Russia recently.
In turn, Russia accuses western countries of spying on it. The FSB has said it exposed 400 foreign agents and 39 Russian spies in 1995 and 1996 alone.
